purpose: Determine whether invocation/completion intervals admit a legal sequential explanation under the simplified idempotent-sink contract.

clock_contract.intervals: start_ns and end_ns use the same monotonic observer clock.
clock_contract.real_time_order: If A.end_ns < B.start_ns, A must precede B. Equal boundaries remain unordered because clock resolution may be ambiguous.
clock_contract.limitation: Do not compare raw timestamps from unsynchronized hosts. A distributed exporter must provide a justified clock mapping with uncertainty bounds or causal/happens-before data.

abstract_contract: A committed operation binds a key to a request/effect/policy intent and observed effect/receipt identifiers.
A committed retry with the same key and intent returns the same effect and receipt identifiers.
A different intent under an existing key may return key_conflict but must not commit.
An unknown result may be unprocessed, may reserve the key without an effect, or may have committed with identifiers not observed by the caller.
Distinct keys cannot reuse an observed effect ID or receipt ID.
A witness must respect strict real-time precedence for non-overlapping intervals and every transition in the sequential model.

status_semantics.LINEARIZABLE: A concrete witness was found within the bounded search.
status_semantics.NON_LINEARIZABLE: Exhaustive bounded search found no legal witness for this finite trace and model.
status_semantics.INVALID_HISTORY: Input malformed or outside the frozen protocol.

explicit_non_claims: Does not authenticate trace records or prove operations were not omitted.
Does not prove sink durability, distributed consensus, or production correctness.
A result applies only to the supplied finite history and simplified contract.
Search-limit exhaustion is inconclusive, never a pass or failure.
Raw timestamps from unsynchronized hosts are invalid for this protocol.
